author: Clement Cherlin
html:
I find your arguments about null unconvincing. They seem to boil down to Java has null, and Java is good, so null is good, and NullPointerException is good.

“If you could have initialized the value to begin with then why didn’t you do it?”
Because Java doesn’t make you, because Java has null (bad design), and fields default to mutable (bad design) and mutable reference fields default to null if not explicitly assigned (more bad design). The ubiquity of static analysis tools for nullness is a cost, not a benefit. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parable_of_the_broken_window

author: Cedric Dandoy
html:
Excellent article.
I think the reason many people hate checked exceptions is because they add noise without value. FP made it even worse.
It does not matter if your persistence layer throws a SQLException, MongoException, IOException, SocketException or NullPointerException.
In the end, the user must be informed that something didn’t work, the code needs to cleanup, and the developer needs the stack trace.
